title: Valid Perfect Square
prompt: Given a positive integer `num`, return `true` if `num` is a perfect square, and `false` otherwise. You may not use any built-in library function such as `sqrt`.
hints: Incrementing a counter and squaring it until you reach or pass num works, but takes O(sqrt(num)) time.
Since k*k grows monotonically with k, binary search on candidate roots in the range [1, num] instead of scanning linearly.
At each mid, compare mid*mid to num: if equal, it's a perfect square; if smaller, search higher; if larger, search lower.

solution.approach: Binary search over possible roots from 1 to num. Because mid*mid is monotonically increasing in mid, comparing mid*mid to num tells you unambiguously which half of the range to keep. If low and high converge without ever finding mid*mid == num, num is not a perfect square. This turns an O(sqrt(num)) scan into an O(log num) search.
